content:
Let the triangle have vertices \((0,0),(7,0),(0,7)\), so the hypotenuse is \(x+y=7\).  
The only non-horizontal/non-vertical drawn line is this hypotenuse, so every triangle must use part of it as one side. Its other two sides must be one horizontal and one vertical grid line.

If those two grid lines meet at a lattice point \((a,b)\), then the endpoints on the hypotenuse are \((7-b,b)\) and \((a,7-a)\). This forms a nondegenerate triangle exactly when
\[
a+b<7.
\]
Thus each valid triangle corresponds to an integer lattice point \((a,b)\) with \(a,b\ge 0\) and \(a+b\le 6\).

Count these points:
\[
\sum_{s=0}^{6}(s+1)=1+2+\cdots+7=28.
\]

\[
\boxed{28}
\]
